name: Len Blavatnik
sec_insider_companies: LyondellBasell Industries N.V. (LYB) - TenPercentOwner; Disc Medicine, Inc. (IRON) - TenPercentOwner; Hemab Therapeutics Holdings, Inc. (COAG) - TenPercentOwner; Upstream Bio, Inc. (UPB) - TenPercentOwner; DigitalOcean Holdings, Inc. (DOCN) - Other
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Wikidata (2019); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Born in Ukraine, raised north of Moscow, Len Blavatnik immigrated to the U.S. in 1978 with his family; he studied computer science at Columbia University and received an MBA from Harvard Business School.
He made an early fortune from Russian oil company TNK-BP, including billions in dividends paid by the joint venture and the sale of his stake in 2013 for $7 billion.
After purchasing Warner Music in 2011 for $3.3 billion, he took the company public in June 2020 at quadruple the value.
His investment firm Access Industries holds stakes in chemicals firm LyondellBasell, energy conglomerate Calpine and house flipping website Opendoor.
Blavatnik says he has given or pledged over $1 billion to philanthropy, mostly to universities, including Oxford, Stanford, Harvard and Yale.
He is a dual citizen of the U.S. and the U.K.
forbes_facts: Blavatnik bought artist Damien Hirst's giant gilded wooly mammoth skeleton entitled "Gone (but) Not Forgotten" for $15 million in 2014.
Blavatnik has been a producer on several Broadway shows including "The Front Page" and "Sunset Boulevard."

name: Gao Guangrong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2020-2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Gao Guangrong is the chairman of Eoptolink Technology, a leading supplier of optical modules in China.
He got his start as a technician at Leshan Radio Company, based in Sichuan province, in 1989.
Gao cofounded the company with five others in 2008 and took it public in 2016.

name: Dan Wilks
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2021); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Dan and his brother Farris got a combined $3.5 billion (pretax) in 2011 selling their fracking company to a group led by Singapore-based firm Temasek.
The brothers have acquired more than 672,000 acres of land in six different states across the West, becoming America's 12th-largest landowners.
They first founded Wilks Masonry in 1995, following in their stone mason father's footsteps.
In 2002 they went into fracking, launching Frac Tech and growing it into an oil and natural gas giant before cashing out less than a decade later.
The brothers are also investing in oil and gas businesses, including fracking company U.S. Well Services and data provider Dawson Geophysical Company.
forbes_facts: Dan Wilks and his brother are active Republican donors.
The brothers reportedly spend four months a year in Montana, working on building homes on their  large ranches.

name: Filippo Ghirelli
forbes_bio: Filippo Ghirelli is a Monaco-based Italian businessman with investments in infrastructure, real estate and energy.
In 2024 he launched Infracorp, an investment firm focused on energy, transportation, decentralized AI and commercial space flight, including orbital modules and data centers.
He also has significant investments in oil & gas infrastructure.
He founded and led Genera Group, an Italian energy efficiency firm, from 2009 until 2024, when he sold the company to Swiss investment manager SUSI Partners.
Through his family office, Sophrance Global, Ghirelli also invests in oil & gas, real estate and edtech startups.

name: Gim Seong-gon
forbes_bio: Gim Seong-gon is the chairman of CS Wind, a maker of wind towers, which he founded in 1988.
In 2008, Goldman Sachs invested around $40 million in the company, allowing it to expand into other markets.
CS Wind now has operations in China, Indonesia, Korea, Malaysia, Taiwan, Turkey and Vietnam.
Gim, who grew up poor, worked at a local construction company and opted to be stationed in its Saudi Arabia branch for a higher salary.
He later set up a trading company for construction materials in Saudi Arabia before his foray into wind towers.
forbes_facts: CS Wind gets its name from "ChoonSan," a pen name for Gim's son, Chang-hon, which means "a heavy mountain that can endure every hardship."
